title: Wireless Security Foundations
description: Why radio changes the threat model: broadcast medium, no physical boundary, layer-1 evidence, and the legal boundary of testing.
objectives: Explain why 802.11 traffic can be observed without any network access and what that means for a penetration test
Distinguish Wi-Fi (802.11) from other wireless technologies and say why the academy stays focused on 802.11
Describe the engagement lifecycle used by every later module: authorisation → recon → enumeration → test → evidence → impact → remediation → retest → report
State the legal and ethical limits: own lab hardware or a signed authorisation, never third-party networks
artifacts: Lab review: read the sample Rules of Engagement in Engagement Mode and list what is in scope
evidence_focus: Every finding must name the affected BSSID/SSID and the frame or config line that proves it.
retest_focus: A retest is only credible if the original evidence can be reproduced byte-for-byte (same capture hash, same filter).

lessons.title: Why wireless changes the threat model

title: Wi-Fi Fundamentals: Identity and Topology
description: SSID vs BSSID vs ESS, BSS/DS topology, bands and channels, and how to read a beacon without guessing.
objectives: Decode a beacon's fixed fields and identify SSID, BSSID, channel, capability and beacon interval
Explain the difference between an ESS, a BSS and a BSSID and why the distinction matters for recon evidence
Map 2.4/5/6 GHz channels, channel width and overlap, and choose a capture channel
Describe what a client leaks in a probe request (PNL, wildcard probes, randomised MAC)
evidence_focus: Extract frame numbers, BSSID, channel and SSID text exactly as captured; keep the capture hash.
retest_focus: Re-run the same tshark filter after a fix so the before/after evidence uses identical extraction.

lessons.title: Identity, topology and reading a beacon

title: 802.11 Frames, IEs and the Association Flow
description: Management/control/data frames, the information elements that carry security policy, and the association state machine.
objectives: Identify frame type/subtype numbers and pick the right display filter for each
Read RSNE fields: version, group cipher, pairwise ciphers, AKM suites and RSN capabilities (including MFPC/MFPR bits)
Walk the association flow and explain what each step proves
Explain what a client must accept for a downgrade to succeed (transition mode, missing PMF, weak AKM)
evidence_focus: Frame numbers + the decoded IE values (not screenshots of text you typed).
retest_focus: Compare the RSNE before and after a configuration change to show the policy actually changed.

lessons.title: Frames, information elements and the association flow

title: Monitor Mode and the Wireless Toolchain
description: Interface modes, monitor mode and injection, driver/firmware reality, and choosing the right tool for each job.
objectives: Explain which interface modes are needed for capture vs. injection and why managed mode cannot see other networks' frames
Verify adapter capability (monitor/injection, supported bands) instead of assuming it
Read the regulatory domain with `iw reg get` and understand why setting it is a jurisdiction decision, not a troubleshooting step
Decide when the lab can be completed with a capture (SIMULATION) and when real radio hardware is required (RF_REQUIRED)
artifacts: labs: none (hardware-facing). Uses lab-data summaries to practise interface reasoning.
evidence_focus: Interface name, mode, channel and driver evidence from your own machine (`iw dev`, `iw phy`) when hardware is used.
retest_focus: Repeat the interface check after a driver or mode change and record both outputs.

lessons.title: Monitor mode, injection and the toolchain

title: Passive Reconnaissance and ESS Mapping
description: Enumerate BSSs, clients and relationships from a passive capture, and separate a legitimate ESS from a look-alike.
objectives: Produce an AP inventory (BSSID, SSID, channel, band, security, PMF, WPS) from a capture
Explain why hiding an SSID is not a security control and show the frame that reveals it
Reconstruct client behaviour: what it probes for, where it associates, whether the MAC is randomised
Identify look-alike infrastructure by comparing IE fingerprints, channels and vendor OUIs
evidence_focus: AP inventory table + frame numbers for every claim; capture SHA-256.
retest_focus: Re-run the inventory after remediation and show the look-alike BSSID is gone from the authorised list.

title: Traffic Analysis: From Capture to Evidence
description: Filter, isolate and extract the exact frames that prove a finding — the core skill behind every later report.
objectives: Write display filters that target management subtypes, EAPOL/EAP, RADIUS and BSSID/SSID
Isolate one conversation and reconstruct the association + 4-way handshake with frame numbers
Recognise what is and is not visible on the air (encrypted payload vs. metadata)
Package evidence: capture hash, filter, frame list, and the claim each frame supports
evidence_focus: A reproducible filter string plus frame numbers, capture SHA-256, and a statement of what the evidence does *not* show.
retest_focus: Same filter re-run on the post-fix capture; the delta is the retest evidence.

title: WEP: Why the Design Fails
description: RC4 with a 24-bit IV, CRC32 integrity and why key recovery is a matter of minutes — plus the migration path.
objectives: Explain IV reuse and how FMS/KoreK/PTW recover the key from a capture
Explain why the ICV (CRC32) cannot detect modification
State the correct remediation: remove WEP, do not 'harden' it
Describe what evidence a WEP finding needs (frame counts, key recovery proof)
artifacts: labs: wep-legacy lab notes + generated capture guidance
evidence_focus: IV/frame counts, the recovered key *in the lab only*, and the tool output with parameters.
retest_focus: Post-fix capture shows no WEP BSS and the network no longer accepts WEP association.

title: WPA2/RSN: Key Hierarchy and the 4-Way Handshake
description: PMK → PTK → KCK/KEK/TK, the M1–M4 exchange, GTK delivery, and where the design is actually strong or weak.
objectives: Derive PMK/PTK and explain each field the PTK is bound to
Identify M1–M4 in a capture and say what each message proves
Explain why capturing a handshake does not mean the network is compromised
Read RSN capabilities and set/verify PMF (MFPC vs MFPR)
artifacts: labs: wpa2-handshake.pcapng (two clients, one complete exchange)
evidence_focus: The handshake's frame numbers, nonces (first/last bytes are enough), capture hash, and the wordlist/params used.
retest_focus: After a PSK change, the old capture must no longer crack and the new one must.

title: Offline Audit: Handshake and PMKID
description: Converting a capture to hashcat material, running an authorised audit, and stating what a cracked PSK does and does not prove.
objectives: Convert a capture with hcxpcapngtool and run hashcat mode 22000 (unified PMKID + EAPOL)
Compare clientless PMKID capture with a 4-way handshake capture (requirements, completeness)
Interpret a crack: what access does the key actually grant?
Write the finding with defensible severity derived from impact, not from the technique name
evidence_focus: Hashcat potfile/`--show` output, the hc22000 file hash, the capture hash, and the recovery duration/rate.
retest_focus: Re-run the same conversion after the PSK changes: the line must be gone from `--show` output.

title: WPS: The 8-Digit PIN and Its Defences
description: WPS architecture, the 11 000-guess PIN flaw, registrar/setup-locked states, and why disabling WPS beats tuning lockout.
objectives: Decode the WPS IE: version, config methods, device password ID, setup-locked, selected registrar
Explain the 10^7 → ~11 000 reduction and what defeats it (lockout, M4/M6 validation, WPS 2.0)
Explain why 'WPS enabled' is a configuration finding while the PIN attack itself needs an authorization decision
Remediate: disable WPS, or if it must exist, enforce lockout and use PBC with a monitored window
evidence_focus: Beacon frame number, decoded WPS attributes, and AP model/firmware if known.
retest_focus: Post-fix beacon shows no WPS IE (or setup-locked + lockout logs) and a new enumeration attempt fails.

lessons.title: WPS architecture and the PIN flaw

title: WPA3: SAE, Transition Mode and OWE
description: SAE (Dragonfly) handshake properties, forward secrecy, transition-mode downgrade, PMF requirements and OWE.
objectives: Explain why the SAE commit/confirm exchange is not offline-crackable
Detect transition mode from the RSNE (AKM list) and describe the downgrade path
Explain the PMF requirement and OWE's role for open networks
Judge whether a WPA3 deployment is genuinely WPA3-only
evidence_focus: RSNE bytes and frame numbers for the AKM list; a client-side association trace showing which AKM was used.
retest_focus: Re-enumerate the BSS after forcing WPA3-only and verify the PSK AKM is gone.

title: Management Frame Protection and Availability
description: Unauthenticated management frames, reason codes, SA Query, and how PMF changes what an attacker can do.
objectives: Explain why unprotected deauth/disassoc frames can be spoofed and what that achieves
Read MFPC/MFPR from the RSNE and predict whether spoofing will work
Interpret reason codes (1, 7, 8, 15) and SA Query behaviour
Assess availability impact as a finding (and why it is often the weakest but noisiest test)
artifacts: labs: deauth.pcapng (PMF-capable vs PMF-required BSS), wpa3-only.pcapng
evidence_focus: Frame numbers, reason codes, counts and timing; plus client-side evidence (association loss) that the frames had effect.
retest_focus: With ieee80211w=2 the same spoof no longer disconnects the client — capture both states.

title: Rogue Infrastructure and Evil Twin
description: How rogue APs are built, why clients join them, and how to distinguish a rogue twin from legitimate infrastructure.
objectives: Compare IE fingerprints, BSSID vendor/OUI, channel, beacon interval and signal to identify a twin
Explain client behaviour that makes evil twin practical (auto-connect, PNL, missing server validation)
Describe detection controls (WIDS/WIPS, authorised-BSSID lists, RF triangulation) and their limits
Design the test safely: which SSIDs are authorised, and what must never be captured from real clients
evidence_focus: Rogue BSSID + frame numbers, twin vs. legitimate IE diff, and client association evidence.
retest_focus: WIDS raises the rogue BSSID and the client no longer associates to the unauthorised infrastructure.

title: Captive Portals, Guest Networks and Isolation
description: Portal architecture, session handling weaknesses, and client isolation as a control rather than a checkbox.
objectives: Trace the portal flow (DHCP → DNS/HTTP redirect → portal → session) from a capture
Identify credential exposure when the portal is served over cleartext HTTP
Test whether client isolation is enforced, and explain the difference between isolation and segmentation
Remediate with HTTPS portal, OWE/WPA2-Guest, per-client isolation and VLAN + ACL enforcement
evidence_focus: HTTP request/response frame numbers, session token, and an ARP/ICMP test showing whether peers are reachable.
retest_focus: Isolation enabled: the repeat test shows no client-to-client reachability; capture both states.

title: Enterprise Wi-Fi: 802.1X Architecture
description: The full enterprise path: client → 802.11 → authenticator (AP) → EAP → RADIUS → identity store, and where the trust boundaries are.
objectives: Draw the 802.1X architecture and name the role of supplicant, authenticator and authentication server
Explain how the MSK becomes the PMK and why the 4-way handshake still happens after EAP succeeds
List the attributes RADIUS returns (VLAN, ACL, session timeout) and the risks of trusting them
Identify the testing decision points for each enterprise component
evidence_focus: EAP exchange frames, RADIUS code + attributes, and the resulting 4-way handshake — in one timeline.
retest_focus: After remediation, re-capture and show the client can no longer authenticate with the old configuration (e.g. missing certificate validation).

title: EAP Methods and Credential Exposure
description: PEAP, EAP-TLS, EAP-TTLS and MS-CHAPv2: what each method protects, what it leaks, and what a rogue authenticator can capture.
objectives: Identify the EAP method from the outer exchange and explain what is inside the tunnel
Explain MS-CHAPv2 challenge/response and why it is crackable when the server's certificate is not validated
Compare EAP-TLS (mutual certificates) with password-based inner methods
Advise on client configuration: ca_cert, domain_suffix_match/subject_match, and disabling insecure methods server-side
evidence_focus: EAP method, outer/inner identity, TLS record frame numbers, and (lab only) the crackable MS-CHAPv2 values.
retest_focus: With server certificate validation enforced, the rogue authenticator attempt fails and the client logs a validation error.

lessons.title: Certificate validation and the PEAP lab

title: RADIUS: Trust, Secrets and Attributes
description: RADIUS protocol mechanics, verifiable integrity (Message-Authenticator/Response Authenticator), and the shared-secret problem.
objectives: Decode an Access-Request/Challenge/Accept exchange and name the attributes that matter
Verify a Message-Authenticator and a Response Authenticator from a capture
Explain why the shared secret is a high-value credential and how it is attacked (offline guessing against captured authenticators)
Harden: per-AP secrets, require_message_authenticator, source-IP restriction, RadSec, and monitoring
artifacts: labs: radius.pcapng (including a rogue NAS whose Message-Authenticator fails)
evidence_focus: The RADIUS packet bytes/hex for the verifiable attributes, the secret used (lab), and the calculation performed.
retest_focus: Rotate the secret and re-verify: the old capture no longer validates against the new secret.

title: Corporate Wireless Kill Chains
description: How individual weaknesses chain into network access: rogue authenticator, credential capture, segmentation bypass — and how each link is broken.
objectives: Assemble a defensible attack chain from the evidence you collected in earlier modules
Test segmentation and isolation with a method whose result is unambiguous (protocol-level reachability, not 'it felt open')
Map each link in the chain to a specific control that breaks it
Report the chain without overstating impact: access to a VLAN is not 'domain admin'
evidence_focus: One timeline: deauth/rogue frames, EAP capture, credential material, and the segmentation test result with frame numbers.
retest_focus: Post-fix: each link is re-tested individually and shown to fail.

title: Wireless VAPT Methodology and Reporting
description: The professional wrapper: scope and RoE, test sequencing, evidence standards, severity from impact, and retest.
objectives: Turn a scope document into a test plan with explicit in/out-of-scope artefacts
Apply the evidence standard: reproducibility, integrity (hash), and traceability to a claim
Derive severity from a finding's actual impact using CVSS as a calculation, not a label
Write a finding and a retest section a client can act on
evidence_focus: Every claim traceable to a frame number, configuration line, or log entry — plus the integrity hash.
retest_focus: The retest section states the exact test repeated and the observed difference.

lessons.title: Methodology, scope and rules of engagement

title: Final Engagement: Independent Assessment
description: A full authorised engagement: scope, RoE, artefacts, objectives — you decide what to test, what proves it, and what to recommend.
objectives: Run recon → enumeration → targeted testing → evidence → findings → remediation → retest planning without step-by-step guidance
Produce a client-ready report with prioritised findings and an explicit retest plan
Defend each finding against the evidence and remove anything you cannot reproduce
Identify what you did *not* test and why (scope, safety, or environment limits)
evidence_focus: Engagement report with an evidence appendix: capture hashes, filters, frame numbers, config excerpts, and retest steps.
retest_focus: The report's retest section is executed against the remediated artefacts and the result recorded.
